reviews.comment: Smart professor but is clearly very wrapped up with his research and does not have time to teach. slides are just the textbook copy and pasted and extremely complex/long. Midterm Final and Labs only and his tests are incredibly detailed and hard plus mostly free response. Usually late to class. I have never had a class this stressful. had to drop
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very fair grader and approachable. Labs are extremely detailed and loaded, but manageable, so get started early and don't be afraid to ask questions. Lectures and exams are also very technical so take advantage of office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
He is very friendly & approachable but unfortunately the lecture is mind-numbing. He clearly knows his stuff but will ramble on about small details. Slides get posted, tests are online. Labs are manageable, 8 total, deadlines are spread out, also a bit mind-numbing. Only grades are midterm, final, & labs. 
Don't take unless you need the credit!!!

just an overall awful class. professor is great and resourceful, but the class is possibly the least practical use of your time ever if you have to take this. total slog and exams are ridiculous if you don't eat, breathe, and sleep remote sensing.

Filippi was friendly and knowledgeable, his class was horrible though. He clearly knows what he is talking about but sometimes forgets that we are not remote sensing experts and tends to lose students attention during lecture with his technical rants. Labs are the worst and take at least 4 hours. ENVI is trash.

Smart dude. Okay professor. Lectures consisted of talking about 1-3 slides for 50 minutes personally didn't learn much that way, but if you do the readings and know what to study for the exams you should be okay. PS labs are arguably very difficult. ASK for help if you need it, no shame in it.

He is a kind, knowledgeable professor who is certainly qualified to be at TAMU. That being said, he is not great at teaching the material. His slides were 100+ slides long for many of the chapters, and I usually found myself lost or not paying attention because he talked a lot yet seemed to not cover all of the content. Exams are comprehensive.

I wouldn't recommend taking this class for fun unless you have a deeply rooted passion for remote sensing. Don't get me wrong, Dr. Filippi knows his stuff, but he goes through the material insanely fast. Labs are fine but there are times when they become very long and time consuming. 2 exams and 10 labs are the only grades you get in this class.

He FLIES through material, making it hard to take down necessary notes. Nevertheless, he still did not get to multiple topics, and held students responsible for watching lectures on those topics, outside of class time. Some test questions were quite specific, so expect to memorize large amounts of technical information.
Good professor. Bad class. If you aren't good with GIS programs, take another class if possible. We use ENVI and it's literally the worst. Again, nothing against the proff.
His lectures were messy & pretentious. The labs didn't help. Tests were filled with short answer & blank pages to illustrate diagrams from memory. Not clear. Didn't make his own lectures.

If you have to take this class for credit just be prepared. There's so much information being thrown at you and lab can get extremely tricky and annoying. The midterm and final are insane, but if you try your best in this class, do good on the labs, you should pass. Just don't give up. Dr. Filippi is a great professor and really knows his stuff.
